links.comparator_used: Fixed monitors with a pre-specified discrepancy measure, at the same false-alarm level (not periodic labeled audits)
links.outcome: Speed of shift detection at matched false-alarm level (average run length) in unstructured data streams, including clinical AI scribe data
links.effect: Adaptive monitors detected shifts faster than fixed monitors across three real-world datasets; LLM-concept monitors were fastest when shifts were sparse and interpretable. No numeric detection delays are given in the text. Calibration sets as small as m=30 gave effective false-alarm control.
links.tradeoff: False-alarm guarantees are only asymptotic and depend on a calibration set of size m drawn from the pre-change distribution. Fixed measures face a sensitivity-breadth trade-off: narrow ones miss unexpected shifts, broad ones lose sensitivity.
links.quote: Across three real-world datasets, including data from a clinical AI scribe deployment, adaptive monitors detect shifts faster than fixed monitors at the same false-alarm level.

design_hint: drift monitoring with adaptive shift detection
